text.p: SOLIDERE shares rose on Thursday and dealers expected the market to further pick up after parliamentary elections end on Sunday.
A shares rose on the privately-operated Beirut Secondary Market (BSM) to $106.875 from Wednesday's $105.5 and B shares rose to $108.5 from $108.
"The momentum is building up because of the success of paliamentary elections and I expect the market to pick up even more after this weekend's last round of elections," a dealer told Reuters.
Dealers say the victory of Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and many of his supporters in the elections has helped boost confidence in the Lebanese economy.
The first four rounds of the five-stage election were held on the past four Sundays amid widespread accusations of fraud but without serious violence. The Bekaa valley votes on Sunday.
On the Beirut Stock Exchange, there was trade in only Ciments Libanais which rose to $1.375 each from $1.31 on sale of 500 shares.
"During the past month an upward trend has developed in the price of Ciments Libanais shares," the dealer added.
There was no trade in any of the other three listed companies, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
Turnover on the BSM, which trades only SOLIDERE shares, fell to 5,306 shares from 7,206 on Wednesday and value was $564,862 from $767,653.
The BLOM Stock Index which covers both markets rose 1.48 percent to 936.63 and the LISPI index rose 0.92 percent to 83.78.
